subject: Response guarantees and escalation credit structure — proposal review
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan@brightline.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Response guarantees + credits question for Dedicated pilot

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team at Brightline is aligned on using Redwood Dedicated for our inference tiering but procurement needs clarity on two items before we move to PO:

1) How exactly do you calculate incident credits for availability misses? We have a mixed workload (80% inference, 20% batch) and need a predictable formula.
2) Can you confirm the escalation windows (on-call, paging cadence) that map to the 99.9 vs 99.95 bands? Our SREs will require an ops runbook for handoffs.

Attached is our procurement checklist; it calls for an explicit credit schedule and a 30-day pilot discount if acceptable. Can you share an official matrix and an example calculation for a multi-region failover event?

Thanks —
Ethan
Ops Lead, Brightline AI
attachments: Brightline-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@brightline.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Response guarantees + credits question for Dedicated pilot

Ethan — great questions, and thanks for the checklist. I attached the current SLA matrix (redwood-sla-matrix-v3.pdf) and a worked example at the bottom of this email. High-level notes:

- Credit calc: we use a sliding penalty by uptime band measured per billing period. For Dedicated pilots we can provide a simplified pro-rata credit: credit = (SLO_target - observed_uptime) * committed_monthly_fee * multiplier_by_severity. Example in attachment uses a 3x multiplier for P1 incidents that impact inference throughput.

- Escalation windows: 99.95 band includes a 30-minute initial pager for P1s (24/7) and a 2-hour acknowledgement target for P2 weekdays; 99.9 has a 1-hour initial pager. We include a documented on-call rotation, escalation contacts, and a handoff checklist in the runbook.

- Pilot discount: we commonly offer a 30% pilot discount on Dedicated reserving for the first 30 days in exchange for a short acceptance test plan (we'll propose a 7-day ramp + 14-day test).

I'll ask Naomi to surface any legal/finance constraints and Kim to confirm the post-incident timelines we propose for RCA/postmortem delivery. If that sounds reasonable, I'll put together a short mutual action plan and an annotated contract excerpt you can share with procurement.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-sla-matrix-v3.pdf (PDF)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Response guarantees + credits question for Dedicated pilot

On Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 10:45 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ethan — great questions...

Quick operational tweaks from my side (internal):

- Escalation cadence: suggest we tighten the P2 weekday acknowledgement to 1 hour rather than 2 for the pilot; reduces ambiguity for Brightline's SREs and keeps the pilot experience high.

- RCA timeline: propose 48 hours for an initial incident summary (facts, impact window, mitigations) and 7 business days for a full RCA for Sev1/P1. That aligns with our postmortem SLAs for Dedicated customers.

- Credit math: let's include an illustrative multi-region failover example where one region degrades to 95% for 4 hours and we show the resulting credit across the committed fee, with the P1 multiplier called out. Jordan — please include that exact table in the contract excerpt.

I'll draft the short-runbook snippet we can embed as an appendix (on-call contacts, paging policy, switchover checklist). Naomi, any finance/legal flags on the 30% pilot discount?

— Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kim / Naomi —

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the matrix. The credit calculation example looks good; the multi-region failover table answered the procurement team's main concern. A couple of remaining asks from legal/procurement: 1) can Brightline get a 45-day invoice term during the pilot, and 2) a one-time 15% signing credit if we commit to a 6-month reserved block after the pilot completes.

If Redwood can confirm those two items, procurement is comfortable moving to a PO and we can sign the pilot SOW this week. We can run the acceptance test plan you suggested.

Thanks —
Ethan
